newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal sector reaches another regional deal.
newsitem.headline: German metal sector reaches another regional deal.

text.p: Engineering employers and the IG Metall union in west Berlin on Wednesday reached an accord guaranteeing continued full sick pay and a modest pay rise, matching deals in other regions of the German metal sector, employers said.
The deal covers some 100,000 workers and prevents the implementation of an unpopular law allowing firms to cut sick pay by 20 percent.
It also sets pay rises of 1.5 percent from January 1, 1997 followed by a 2.5 percent rise from April 1, 1998, the VME regional employers' association said in a statement.
The Christmas bonus will be cut by five percentage points to 55 percent of monthly pay.
Employers in the engineering industry and other sectors like chemicals and banking have been unable to push through the sick pay cuts in the face of fierce worker resistance.
